architecture_summary.operational_context: Cloud-native CI/CD pipeline using GitHub Actions for build/test, Artifactory for artifact storage, and staged deployment to cloud environments. Secrets managed via dedicated secrets manager. Deploy keys control production access.

threat_actors.name: External Opportunistic Attacker
threat_actors.motivation: Credential theft, cryptomining, supply chain compromise for downstream impact
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Phishing developer credentials or exploiting public GitHub repository misconfigurations
non_capabilities: No physical access to developer workstations
No pre-existing insider knowledge of pipeline internals
No zero-day exploits for GitHub Actions or Artifactory
No ability to compromise upstream dependencies directly

threat_actors.name: Malicious Insider (Compromised Developer)
threat_actors.motivation: Intellectual property theft, sabotage, backdoor insertion
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Legitimate developer credentials with write access to repository
non_capabilities: Cannot bypass branch protection rules without admin approval
Cannot access production deploy keys directly
Cannot modify secrets manager policies without elevated IAM role

threat_actors.name: Supply Chain Attacker
threat_actors.motivation: Inject malicious code into artifacts consumed by downstream users
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Compromise of third-party dependency or build toolchain
non_capabilities: No direct access to GitHub repository or Actions runners
Cannot access secrets manager or deploy key store
No ability to promote artifacts to staging/production without pipeline execution

attack_paths.entry_point: Developer credential phishing or token theft
attack_paths.impact: Full read/write access to source code, ability to push malicious commits, modify workflow files
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Developer credentials are high-value targets; phishing and token leakage are common

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised developer account with repo admin rights
attack_paths.impact: Bypass required reviews and status checks, merge malicious code directly to protected branches
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires admin-level compromise; branch protection misconfigurations are exploitable

attack_paths.entry_point: Malicious workflow file or compromised dependency in build
attack_paths.impact: Arbitrary code execution on runner, access to secrets manager, ability to exfiltrate data or poison artifacts
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Self-hosted or ephemeral runners execute untrusted code; supply chain compromises are increasing

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised Actions runner with access to secrets
attack_paths.impact: Theft of API keys, database passwords, cloud credentials used in pipeline
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Runners need secrets access; malicious workflow steps can dump environment variables

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised Actions runner publishing malicious artifact
attack_paths.impact: Poisoned artifacts deployed to staging/production, affecting downstream consumers
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires successful runner compromise; artifact signing and verification can mitigate

attack_paths.entry_point: Malicious code designed to evade static analysis rules
attack_paths.impact: SAST scanner fails to detect vulnerabilities, allowing vulnerable code to proceed to artifact storage
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires deep knowledge of SAST rules; evasion techniques exist but are complex

attack_paths.impact: Persistence in staging environment, lateral movement to production, data exfiltration
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Staging often has production-like data and network access; promotion gates may be weak

attack_paths.entry_point: Promoted malicious artifact from staging or compromised deploy key
attack_paths.impact: Persistent backdoor in production, full control over production workloads and data
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires bypassing staging validation and deploy key controls; high impact but multiple barriers

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised staging environment with network access to deploy key store
attack_paths.impact: Theft of production deployment keys, ability to deploy arbitrary code to production
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Deploy key store should be network-isolated; requires staging compromise plus lateral movement

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised read-only token or public repository exposure
attack_paths.impact: Exfiltration of source code, architecture details, hardcoded secrets, pipeline configuration
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Repositories often contain sensitive configuration; token scopes may be excessive

mitigations.control_name: Identities and credentials are issued, managed, verified, revoked, and audited
Access permissions and authorizations are managed, incorporating least privilege and separation of duties
Establish and Maintain an Inventory of Accounts
A baseline configuration of information technology/industrial control systems is created and maintained
Ensure That All Application Software is Developed In-House or Acquired from Trusted Sources
Establish and Maintain a Secure Configuration Process for Network Infrastructure
Monitoring for unauthorized personnel, connections, devices, and software is performed
A vulnerability management plan is developed and implemented
Ensure That All Software Development Personnel Receive Training in Writing Secure Code

findings.severity_rationale: Compromised developer credentials grant full pipeline control with high likelihood and no MFA enforcement on all accounts
Branch protection bypass allows direct malicious code merge; admin compromise is feasible via credential theft
Actions runner executes untrusted code with access to all pipeline secrets; supply chain compromise likelihood is high
Malicious artifact publication poisons supply chain; artifact signing not enforced
SAST evasion possible but requires sophisticated attacker; defense-in-depth reduces impact
Staging environment compromise enables lateral movement to production; network segmentation incomplete
Source code exfiltration via excessive token scopes; impacts IP confidentiality but not integrity
